notes: §1985:VI.6.12.3 SR2: "Routine-name-1 is a COBOL word and it may be referred to only in an ENTER sentence." The ENTER statement is not provided at --std 85 (§1985:I.1.5.2.5.5, the implementor's option; kb/Work PB5308): StatementBinder.BindEnter refuses every ENTER with COBOL7240 and declares nothing, so no routine-name-1 exists to be referred to anywhere, and a reference to the word outside ENTER resolves to nothing (COBOL1639). routineName (cobolWord | reservedGatedWord) keeps a later-edition verb word in the slot parsing whole so the refusal lands once at the statement. Probed at --std 85 (classes b, c): ENTER FORTRAN SUB1. followed by GO TO SUB1 draws COBOL7240 then COBOL1639; ENTER FORTRAN FREE. is refused once with COBOL7240; a literal operand is a syntax error; at 2002 COBOL0902 is added. The PB5178 census and period arms the prior PARTIAL named are moot (answers kb/Work PB5539 for this row). The witness refuses GO TO SUBRTN after ENTER FORTRAN SUBRTN. with COBOL1639. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5308 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-07-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Routine-name-1 is a COBOL word and it may be referred to only in an ENTER sentence."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the ENTER statement; the statement and routine-name-1 are dropped.". No 2023 clause holds the ENTER feature, and no worded candidate covers routine-name-1 or the ENTER sentence. The statement is absent from 2023, so the rule is dropped.
